evals.name: cli-banner
evals.prompt: Make a startup banner for my command-line tool PULSE (it tails and colours log files). I want big block letters spelling PULSE, the tagline 'watch your logs breathe' under them, and a border around the whole thing. Pure ASCII only (no Unicode), at most 70 columns wide so it fits a narrow terminal. Save it to banner.txt exactly as it should print - no markdown fences, no explanation in the file.
evals.expected_output: banner.txt is a rectangular framed banner: every line the same width, 70 columns or fewer, pure ASCII, no tabs; the letters are block-rendered across several rows with consistent height (not hand-drawn letters of different heights); the tagline appears intact below the letters; the frame has proper corners and nothing touches or overlaps the border

evals.name: readme-mascot
evals.prompt: Draw an ASCII art owl perched on a branch as the mascot for my project 'nightwatch' (a cron monitor). It goes at the top of the README inside a code block, so: pure ASCII, between 10 and 18 rows, no wider than 40 columns, no colour. Save it to owl.txt with nothing else in the file.
evals.expected_output: owl.txt is an original owl: two eyes on the same row and symmetric about a centre column, a beak between/below them, a body wider than it is tall per row (terminal cells are 2:1), ear tufts or brow shoulders, a horizontal branch under it; 10-18 rows, at most 40 columns, pure ASCII, no tabs, no trailing whitespace, no stray characters outside the figure

evals.name: image-to-ascii
evals.prompt: Convert scene.png (in the current directory) to ASCII art for display in a dark-background terminal. Make it exactly 60 columns wide, keep the picture's proportions, use only plain ASCII characters, and save the result to scene.txt (just the art).
evals.expected_output: scene.txt is 60 columns wide with a row count that preserves the image's aspect ratio for 2:1 terminal cells (roughly 20-25 rows), pure ASCII; bright regions of the image (the pale disc top-left, the red block top-right, the right end of the gradient bar) map to dense characters and the dark background to spaces or light characters - i.e. character density correlates with image luminance for a dark terminal
